history.period: 1870 (most sources; one reviewer claims 1902 on Buddha Purnima — unverified)
history.summary: HISTORY DATE FLAG: most sources (inshorts/CSR Journal, velpu) say the temple was founded in 1870 by Ashutosh Mukherjee (Tantric Ashutosh Tarkaratna), a Chorbagan, Kolkata resident who saw the thousand-handed form of Goddess Kali in a dream; one reviewer instead says Ashitosh Mukherjee established it in 1902 on Buddha Purnima. The temple at Olabibitala, Shibpur is famous for its rare ~17-ft idol of Maa Kali with a thousand hands ('Hajar Haat' = thousand hands in Bengali), symbolising her infinite power. The entire vicinity is locally known as 'Hajar Haat Kali Tala'. Buddha Purnima is celebrated each year as the sthapana day with bhog prasad organised by the Mukherjee family. Legend says dacoits once prayed here before their raids.

name: Shri Shri Hajar Haath Kali Mata Temple
town_description: CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV lists town as 'Howrah' (the city), which is correct at city level; the temple is in the Shibpur locality of Howrah city, at Olabibitala/Naora. Shibpur sits across the Hooghly from Kolkata and is home to the Howrah Bridge's southern approaches.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~20 km)
travel.road: At Olabibitala Lane, Naora, Shibpur (Plot No. 16); reach by toto/auto from Mandirtala or the Second Hooghly Bridge; reviewers note no parking for private cars

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; Kali Puja and Buddha Purnima (sthapana day) are the biggest celebrations
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hours conflict across sources (verify): Justdial says 6:00 AM–10:00 PM daily; velpu lists 7:00 AM–1:00 PM and 5:00–9:00 PM; one video source reports puja/aarti at 6:30 AM, 2:00 PM and 8:30 PM
